accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:simultaneous-confidence-edges
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The MMD guarantee is conditional on the supplied simultaneous evaluation-law L1 ratio-error event; no data-driven ratio radius is claimed.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Familywise-valid ancestral-edge discovery holds conditional on the stated first-stage event, with unconditional coverage only after its stated failure probability is added.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: oeq:generated-rank-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The proposed coordinate-rate and expansion are conditional on a uniform C1 first-stage log-ratio contract and, for asymptotic linearity, an additional uniform first-stage representation.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The open statistical target concerns the conditional generated-rank problem on the bounded subclass; it does not assert attainment by an unspecified ratio learner.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 5–6, Theorems 3.2 and 3.4; p. 9, “Identifiability From One Intervention per Node for Any n”
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves the bivariate one-perfect-stochastic-intervention result under its witness condition, proves arbitrary-dimensional identification from paired interventions, and explicitly conjectures the arbitrary-dimensional one-intervention extension because unknown-target alignment has n!−1 possibilities.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3–5, Definition 3.2, Assumption 4.1, and Theorem 4.2; pp. 29–30, Appendix E
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The main CauCA theorem assumes the graph and known intervention targets; one perfect stochastic intervention per node yields componentwise identification, while the appendix notes nonidentifiability with totally unknown targets in a nontrivial graph.

Theorem 5.3 uses a finite-degree polynomial decoder with full-column-rank coefficients and support assumptions to identify each perfectly intervened latent up to shift and scaling; it does not identify the causal DAG.

The result assumes injective differentiable nonlinear mixing but a linear Gaussian latent SCM; unknown single-node perfect-intervention coverage identifies the model, targets, and graph up to permutation and scaling.

The paper studies measurement models, does not assume the hidden-variable count is known, uses at most one unknown intervention per hidden variable, and identifies latent graph structure only under its graphical conditions.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 4, Theorem 5; p. 12, Theorem 7 and Corollary 9
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: For bounded kernels, the paper establishes characteristic/universal-kernel distribution separation and finite-sample concentration of empirical MMD for directly observed independent two-sample inputs.

source_verification_receipts.version: Accessible author manuscript; the cited 2023 Statistics and Probability Letters typeset version was not directly accessible
source_verification_receipts.locator: Sections 2–5, especially the uniform-rate display in Section 4 and conditional-CDF expansion discussion in Section 5
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The accessible manuscript establishes uniform local-linear conditional-CDF bias, rate, and asymptotic-linear results with observed response thresholds and covariates; it does not cover generated log-ratio thresholds and generated conditioning coordinates jointly.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a compact worked three-node decoder trace that computes the ratio graph, conditional ranks, target alignment, and parent-pruning output from the supplied sparse witness.
State a corollary isolating the exact implication from nonzero direct-edge second-moment contrast to Gaussian-MMD cover separation, including the redundant-edge case.
Specify one concrete ratio-learning family and prove or sharply formulate sufficient conditions for its uniform C1(K) contract, so the generated-rank question connects to an attainable first stage.

recommended_next_step: Advance the field-tier proposal to Stage 0; retain the certified witness calculations and the conditional-rank linearization as early proof checkpoints.
